title: Canonical tensor formulas for boundary q
statement:
Let $C$ be a Grothendieck abelian, closed symmetric monoidal coefficient category with additive tensor product, functorial flat resolutions, and flat-preserving etale, pro-etale and comparison inverse images. For a morphism of schemes $i:Z\to T$ use the ordinary derived categories of $C$-valued sheaves on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], and write $C_W=\nu_W^*$ and $F_\tau=Ri_{\tau,*}$ for $\tau=e,p$ [def-weil-boundary-exceptional-comparison-data]. A normalized symmetry presentation is an isomorphism of the derived tensor bifunctor with its flip whose component at every $(K,L)$ is the canonical descended Koszul braiding $\sigma_{K,L}$.

Use the counit-defined projection transformation $\pi^\tau_{B,M}:F_\tau B\otimes^LM\to F_\tau(B\otimes^Li_\tau^*M)$ [def-kun-projection-formula-map], with its fixed-coefficient components and monoidal comparison $c_{W;K,L}:C_W(K\otimes^LL)\cong C_WK\otimes^LC_WL$ as in [lem-weil-boundary-proetale-projection-comparison]. Given an etale adjunction $F_e\dashv G$ and $M,N\in D(T_e,C)$ with $\pi^e_{GN,M}$ invertible, define $q^e_{M,N}:i_e^*M\otimes^LGN\to G(M\otimes^LN)$ as the transpose of
$$F_e(i_e^*M\otimes^LGN)\xrightarrow{F_e(\sigma)}F_e(GN\otimes^Li_e^*M)\xrightarrow{(\pi^e_{GN,M})^{-1}}F_eGN\otimes^LM\xrightarrow{\sigma}M\otimes^LF_eGN\xrightarrow{1\otimes\varepsilon_N}M\otimes^LN.$$
For pro-etale $M,N,B$, a map $\mu:F_pB\to N$, and invertible $\pi^p_{B,M}$, define $t^p:F_p(i_p^*M\otimes^LB)\to M\otimes^LN$ by the identical composite with $B$ in place of $GN$ and $\mu$ in place of $\varepsilon_N$. Define the source isomorphism
$$s_{M,B}:C_Z(i_e^*M\otimes^LB)\xrightarrow{c_Z}C_Zi_e^*M\otimes^LC_ZB\xrightarrow{\rho_M^{-1}\otimes1}i_p^*C_TM\otimes^LC_ZB,$$
where $\rho:i_p^*C_T\cong C_Zi_e^*$ is the canonical pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. The generic assembly helpers compose these arrows with supplied exceptional Hom transport and origin-map families before specializing the coefficient category; they introduce no additional maps in the specialized constructions.
